ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the upper half of the figure is a positively charged iminium/imine skeleton, with C=N+ at the center, the left-side carbon connected to R1 and R2, and the right-side nitrogen connected to R3 and R4; the lower half is a formic acid molecule, with the skeleton H-C(=O)-OH. There are also some curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring them. Then reason: represent the upper R1/R2-C=N+(R3/R4) skeleton with wildcard SMILES as *C(*)=[N+](*)*; represent the lower formic acid as O=CO; finally connect the two mutually independent fragments with a dot, obtaining *C(*)=[N+](*)*.O=CO.

method.method_draft: First describe the image contents: ignore the curved arrows and keep only the atom-bond skeleton. Convert the iminium skeleton R1/R2-C=N+(R3/R4) into wildcard SMILES as *C(*)=[N+](*)*. Then convert the separate formic acid H-C(=O)-OH into O=CO. Join the two disconnected fragments with a dot to obtain *C(*)=[N+](*)*.O=CO.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the straightforward structure-to-SMILES transcription route: identify each drawn molecular fragment and encode the bonds/charge directly, rather than using reaction-mechanism interpretation.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawing as two disconnected chemical components while ignoring all curved arrows: an iminium fragment with a carbon double-bonded to positively charged nitrogen, carbon bearing R1 and R2 substituents, nitrogen bearing R3 and R4 substituents; and a formic-acid fragment drawn as H-C(=O)-O-H.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the requested output is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure and that the arrows should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: generic R substituents are represented by wildcard atoms '*'; a positively charged nitrogen must be bracketed as [N+]; double bonds use '='; branches are placed in parentheses; disconnected fragments are separated with '.'. Hydrogens on the acid are implicit in the SMILES O=CO.
